html:
From 1916 to 1924 the United States occupied the Dominican Republic and ruled it through a military government. Marines landed amid civil war and unpaid foreign debts.

The Americans took over customs, built roads, and disarmed the regional strongmen. Peasant guerrillas in the east, called gavilleros, fought them for years. American sugar companies expanded on lands taken from small farmers.

The occupiers created a new national guard. One of its officers, Rafael Trujillo, rose quickly and seized power six years after the Marines left. The occupation ran alongside the US occupation of Haiti next door, part of the banana wars.
